key_files: core.c (283K — main scheduler logic, task creation/destruction, context switch)
fair.c (329K — CFS implementation, vruntime, load balancing)

threading_concerns.priority_inversion: RT mutexes with priority inheritance prevent starvation
threading_concerns.load_balancing: periodic rebalancing across CPUs, NUMA-aware migration

norms.scheduling_latency: CFS target latency 6ms for 1 runnable task, scales with load
norms.time_slice: dynamic based on weight/nice value, typically 1-100ms

memory_concerns.slab_overhead: per-object metadata, cache coloring for alignment
memory_concerns.fragmentation: compaction daemon runs to defragment physical memory
memory_concerns.oom_handling: OOM killer selects process by badness score

security_concerns.stack_overflow: guard pages between kernel stacks, VMAP_STACK
security_concerns.heap_overflow: SLUB red zones, poisoning, freelist randomization

norms.max_threads_system: limited by available memory for kernel stacks

security_concerns.credential_checks: uid/gid/capabilities verified at every access point

mechanisms.futex: fast userspace mutex (kernel arbitrates contention only)
mechanisms.io_uring: async I/O ring buffer (shared memory + submission/completion queues)

message_passing_concerns.copy_overhead: pipes/sockets copy data; shared memory is zero-copy
message_passing_concerns.ordering_guarantees: FIFO within a single pipe/socket; no cross-channel ordering

security_concerns.resource_limits: per-user limits on queues, segments, semaphores
security_concerns.covert_channels: shared memory timing can leak information

threading_model.softirq_processing: network packets processed in softirq context (NET_RX_SOFTIRQ)
threading_model.per_cpu_backlog: each CPU has its own packet processing queue
threading_model.socket_locking: per-socket spinlock, BH-disabled for protocol processing

security_concerns.input_validation_order: CRITICAL: headers parsed before security hooks fire
buffer_overflow_vectors: SKB linear data vs. paged fragments — length validation essential
IP options parsing — bounded by header length field
TCP options — bounded by data offset field
Fragmentation reassembly — total size checks before allocation

filesystem.vfs_layer: Virtual Filesystem Switch — uniform interface to all filesystems
key_files: namei.c — path resolution (MODIFIED: eperm hook before DAC)

security_concerns.race_conditions: TOCTOU between access check and use — O_NOFOLLOW, openat()
security_concerns.buffer_issues: filename length limited to NAME_MAX (255), path to PATH_MAX (4096)

key_areas: usb/ — USB host controllers, device drivers

security_concerns.dma_attacks: IOMMU required to prevent DMA-based attacks from devices
security_concerns.usb_enumeration: untrusted device descriptors parsed in kernel — length validation critical
security_concerns.ioctl_interface: driver-specific ioctls are common attack surface — bounds checking

security_framework.security_hooks: 200+ LSM hooks throughout kernel (task, file, socket, ipc, etc.)
security_framework.integrity: IMA/EVM — file hash verification and extended attributes

cryptography.algorithms: AES, ChaCha20, SHA-256/512, RSA, ECDH, ECDSA, etc.
cryptography.framework: crypto API with hardware acceleration support (AES-NI)

concerns.side_channels: constant-time implementations required for crypto operations

epmp.purpose: Extended Port Multiplexing Protocol — 64-bit port addressing via port 64444
epmp.threading: TCP listener with per-connection state machine

security.handshake: DH key exchange → RSA auth → AES-256 session
security.frame_validation: magic number check, CRC-32C integrity, sequence ordering
concerns: State machine complexity — ensure all transitions are validated
DH parameter validation — check for small subgroup attacks
Frame length field — must validate before allocation to prevent OOM

hpm.threading: Runs in packet processing path (softirq context)

concerns: Performance impact in hot path — must be fast
False positive rate management
State table memory bounds — per-IP tracking needs limits
Atomic operations needed for per-CPU counters

eperm.purpose: Extended Permission Classes — Trusted (4) and Genius (5) bypass DAC
eperm.integration: Hooked into generic_permission() in fs/namei.c BEFORE standard DAC

security.audit: Supreme-tier access logged for Genius class
concerns: Registry integrity — must survive module reload
Race condition between permission check and class change
Proc interface input validation — UID/class parsing

security.release_gate: Grade 7+ admin only (sudo touch system negamane-release)
concerns: Must be enforced before VFS write path
Direct block device access bypasses filesystem checks
Mount options (remount) could theoretically bypass

user_ko.purpose: Per-user kernel objects with 3-tier memory grain model

security.grain_isolation: Grain 1-2 sandboxed, Grain 3 requires sudo rank 4+
concerns: Module verification for Grain 3 (secure boot)
Resource limits per user (max loaded modules, total memory)
Unload path must be clean (reference counting)
Thermal protection — must respect hardware thermal limits
Power budget tracking — aggregate boost across processes
Process impersonation — verify binary path, not just PID

white_ethics.purpose: System presence module — glow cycle, ethics assertion
white_ethics.threading: Timer-based glow cycle (8-36 hour interval, 2 hour duration)

security.read_only: Status reporting only via /proc, no dangerous operations

usb_swap.purpose: USB mass storage as dynamic swap pagefile

security.safety_checks: Won't touch devices with existing partitions/filesystems
concerns: Swap data confidentiality — data at rest on removable media
Hot-remove handling — must migrate pages before disconnect
Speed validation — reject USB 1.x to prevent performance collapse

usb_fast_dma.purpose: Hardware-direct DMA optimization for USB transfers
usb_fast_dma.threading: Batched interrupts, polled mode for latency-critical paths

concerns: DMA boundary validation — prevent writes outside allocated buffers
Timeout enforcement — polled mode must not spin indefinitely
TRB ring overflow — bounds checking on transfer ring entries

kernel_threads.ksoftirqd: deferred softirq processing when load is high
kernel_threads.migration: per-CPU thread for task migration between CPUs

synchronization_primitives.seqlock: sequence counter lock — writer never blocks, reader retries
synchronization_primitives.futex: fast userspace mutex — kernel mediates contention

locking_hierarchy.rule: always acquire locks in consistent global order to prevent deadlock
locking_hierarchy.validation: CONFIG_PROVE_LOCKING (lockdep) detects ordering violations at runtime
concerns: ABBA deadlock — two locks acquired in opposite order by different paths
Softirq/hardirq context — cannot sleep while holding spinlock
RCU grace period stalls — callbacks blocked too long
Priority inversion — low-priority holder blocks high-priority waiter

internal_kernel.notifier_chains: kernel subsystem event notification (blocking, atomic, raw)

kernel_to_user.io_uring: shared ring buffers for async I/O (zero syscall I/O)
kernel_to_user.mmap: shared memory pages between kernel and userspace

input_validation.INT_001: All network packet length fields validated before memory allocation
input_validation.INT_002: All userspace-provided sizes checked against maximum bounds
input_validation.INT_003: All array indices validated against array size
input_validation.INT_004: All pointer arithmetic checked for wraparound (overflow)
input_validation.INT_005: All string inputs null-terminated or length-bounded
input_validation.INT_006: All ioctl cmd values validated via switch/case (not computed)
input_validation.INT_007: All copy_from_user() sizes validated before the copy
input_validation.INT_008: All file descriptor values validated (0 to NR_OPEN)
input_validation.INT_009: All PID values validated against pid_max

buffer_overflow_prevention.BUF_002: SLAB red zones detect overflows in heap allocations
buffer_overflow_prevention.BUF_003: FORTIFY_SOURCE compile-time and runtime bounds checking
buffer_overflow_prevention.BUF_004: VMAP_STACK — kernel stacks in vmalloc space with guard pages
buffer_overflow_prevention.BUF_006: No variable-length arrays on stack (VLA eliminated since 4.20)
buffer_overflow_prevention.BUF_008: Copy-to/from-user always uses hardened accessor functions
buffer_overflow_prevention.BUF_009: SKB (network buffer) headroom/tailroom validated before push/put
buffer_overflow_prevention.BUF_010: USB descriptor parsing bounds-checked against descriptor length

integer_overflow_prevention.IOF_001: size_t used for all memory sizes (unsigned, platform-width)
integer_overflow_prevention.IOF_003: array_size() / struct_size() for dynamic allocation sizing
integer_overflow_prevention.IOF_004: No signed integer for sizes or counts in allocation paths
integer_overflow_prevention.IOF_005: Network protocol field widths respected (16-bit port, 32-bit seq)
integer_overflow_prevention.IOF_006: Page count multiplied safely (shift, not multiply by 4096)

race_condition_prevention.RCE_001: All shared state protected by identified lock or RCU
race_condition_prevention.RCE_002: TOCTOU in permission checks mitigated by holding references
race_condition_prevention.RCE_003: Atomic operations for reference counts (refcount_t, not atomic_t)
race_condition_prevention.RCE_004: Memory barriers where ordering matters across CPUs
race_condition_prevention.RCE_005: No data races on non-atomic shared variables (KCSAN enforced)
race_condition_prevention.RCE_006: Signal handler safety — only async-signal-safe operations
race_condition_prevention.RCE_007: Double-fetch from userspace prevented (copy once, validate copy)

security_before_processing.concern: Data may be processed/parsed BEFORE security checks complete
security_before_processing.SBP_001: LSM hooks fire BEFORE operation executes (not after)
security_before_processing.SBP_003: Permission checks before file content is read into memory
security_before_processing.SBP_004: Namespace isolation verified before IPC delivery
security_before_processing.SBP_005: Seccomp filter evaluated BEFORE syscall handler runs
security_before_processing.SBP_006: Network: netfilter INPUT chain before socket delivery
security_before_processing.SBP_007: EPMP: handshake authentication BEFORE payload processing
security_before_processing.SBP_008: HPM: packet scoring BEFORE forwarding to application
known_gaps: TCP/IP headers parsed in NIC driver before netfilter — checksum/length already consumed
USB descriptors read into kernel memory before policy can evaluate device
BPF bytecode loaded into kernel before verifier runs (verifier is the gate)
Module binary loaded into memory before signature verification

process_length.description: How long operations should normally take
process_length.page_fault: ~1µs (minor, in page cache) to ~5ms (major, disk fetch)
process_length.module_load: < 1s for normal module, several seconds for large subsystems
process_length.concern: Anything exceeding 10x normal duration suggests attack or malfunction

process_verticality.description: Call stack depth and privilege escalation
privilege_boundaries: Process → Process (signals, IPC — mediated by kernel)
process_verticality.concern: Deep nesting in filesystem (40 symlinks max) or network (IP-in-IP tunnels)

process_breadth.max_concurrent_connections: limited by fd limit and memory (10K-1M typical)
process_breadth.concern: Excessive breadth exhausts memory, file descriptors, or CPU time

input_normality.description: What constitutes normal vs. suspicious input patterns
input_normality.concern: Inputs at or near limits are often probing for off-by-one errors
